adjara-children-folk-ensembles-olympiad-.about:
Every year Adjara's Ministry of Culture holds the Olympiad of Children's Folk Song and Dance Ensembles to showcase traditional Georgian folk song and dance among young people, discover talented performers and let ensembles share new creative work. More than 80 choreographic and choral ensembles with over 2,000 performers take part.

The olympiad runs in stages: selection rounds in every Adjara municipality (in 2026 these took place on 18-23 May, starting with Khulo and Shuakhevi), followed by a final gala concert and awards ceremony. Winning ensembles (Grand Prix and first places) receive prizes such as stage costumes and accessories.

Pupils take part as members of a school, music-school or community folk ensemble; joining a local ensemble in Batumi, Kobuleti, Khelvachauri, Keda, Shuakhevi or Khulo is the way in.
highlights: 80+ ensembles and 2,000+ young performers each year
Rounds in every Adjara municipality
Prizes include stage costumes for winning ensembles
adjara-children-folk-ensembles-olympiad-.eligibility: Children's folk choirs and dance ensembles from the Autonomous Republic of Adjara; individual pupils participate through their ensemble.
how_to_apply: Join a school, music-school or community folk ensemble in Adjara
Ask the ensemble leader to register when the ministry announces the 2027 olympiad (spring)
Perform in the municipal round; top ensembles go on to the final gala

adjara-vocational-students-exchange-gran.about:
Adjara's Ministry of Education and Sport started this programme in 2026 to help vocational students add international experience to their training at home. It funds exchange programmes of at least one month at vocational institutions in EU member states, the UK, USA, Canada, Australia, Japan, Switzerland or Norway; for dual (work-based) programmes, placements can be with employers proposed by the partner colleges' foreign partners.

The grant (up to 5,000 GEL) can cover registration on the exchange programme, housing and utilities, international travel, health insurance, visa costs, food and local transport. Students apply to one of the two partner colleges, the public colleges 'Blacksea' in Batumi and 'Akhali Talgha' in Kobuleti, which select candidates in their own competitions and nominate them to the ministry.

A concrete way for students in hospitality, tourism, IT, construction or other trades in Adjara to train abroad.
highlights: Up to 5,000 GEL per student
Exchanges of 1 month or more in Europe, North America, Japan or Australia
Apply through Blacksea (Batumi) or Akhali Talgha (Kobuleti) college
adjara-vocational-students-exchange-gran.eligibility: Citizens of Georgia registered in Adjara for at least one year before the call, who are vocational students and will take part in an exchange vocational programme of at least one month in an eligible country.
how_to_apply: Read the conditions and regulation on the ministry's page
Contact your college: Blacksea (Batumi, info@blacksea.edu.ge) or Akhali Talgha (Kobuleti, info@kpc.ge)
Apply in the college's competition and, if selected, get nominated to the ministry
Sign the grant agreement and keep receipts for reimbursable costs
adjara-vocational-students-exchange-gran.costs: Grant of up to 5,000 GEL for documented exchange costs.

batumi-artists-international-projects-su.about:
Batumi City Hall's 'Support for Artists' sub-programme funds artists who have been invited to international cultural projects: competitions, festivals and exhibitions abroad or in Georgia. Priority goes to music, audiovisual, fine arts and theatre. Each winner gets a one-off advance of up to 2,000 GEL for travel, visa, insurance and registration costs.

Applications are accepted every month and a working group decides within about ten working days. You need an official invitation or proof of participation, a recommendation letter, a CV and, if available, recordings or images of your work. Applicants under 18 apply with a parent's documents, so the scheme suits music-school pupils and young performers selected for international contests.

It does not pay fees for the competition itself unless they are registration costs, and expenses before the contract are not refunded, so apply as soon as you receive your invitation.
highlights: Up to 2,000 GEL per international event
Priority for music, film, fine arts and theatre
Minors can apply through a parent
batumi-artists-international-projects-su.eligibility: Citizens of Georgia who work as artists in Batumi or are registered in Batumi municipality at the time of application, with an official invitation to an international cultural project. Under-18s apply with a parent's ID and their birth certificate. Documents in Georgian.
how_to_apply: Download the regulation and the 2026 application form from the programme page on batumi.gov.ge
Attach: recommendation letter, CV, passport/ID copy, proof of registration, invitation, bank details and (optional) a CD/portfolio of your work
Submit at Batumi City Hall, 25 Luka Asatiani Street, in any monthly window
If approved sign the contract, travel, then submit the report form
batumi-artists-international-projects-su.costs: Free to apply. Up to 2,000 GEL for travel, visa, insurance and registration fees.

batumi-athletes-tournament-travel-suppor.about:
Under the sub-programme 'Support for the Individual Development of Batumi Athletes', Batumi City Hall co-funds athletes and coaches registered in Batumi who are going to sports tournaments, including international ones. The aim is to help them gain competition experience and raise their level. Each winner receives a one-off advance of up to 4,000 GEL for travel, visa, insurance, hotel, tournament fees and sports equipment.

Applications are accepted every month (except November), and a commission decides within ten working days after the month closes. You need an invitation or proof of entry, a recommendation from the national federation or the Adjara federation of your sport, and proof that part of the cost is covered by you or a sponsor. Minors apply through a parent. Within 30 days after the tournament you submit a short report.

A useful route for young Batumi athletes selected for European or world youth championships whose federations cannot cover all costs.
highlights: Up to 4,000 GEL per tournament
Open to minors through a parent; no upper age limit
Monthly intake with decisions in about 10 working days
batumi-athletes-tournament-travel-suppor.eligibility: Citizens of Georgia registered in Batumi municipality who are athletes or coaches with an invitation to a sports tournament and a recommendation from the Georgian national federation or the Adjara federation of their sport. Applicants under 18 apply with a parent's documents. Documents in Georgian.
how_to_apply: Download the regulation and application form from the programme page on batumi.gov.ge
Prepare: application, CV, passport/ID copy (plus parent's ID and birth certificate for minors), proof of Batumi registration, federation recommendation, invitation, and proof of co-funding
Submit at Batumi City Hall, 25 Luka Asatiani Street, during the monthly window
After approval sign the contract; within 30 days after the tournament submit the programme report
batumi-athletes-tournament-travel-suppor.costs: Free to apply. One-off advance of up to 4,000 GEL for travel, visa, insurance, hotel, entry fees and sports kit; co-funding required.

british-council-georgia-ielts-prep-young.about:
The British Council, which co-owns the IELTS test, offers IELTS preparation courses for young adults at its teaching centre in Tbilisi. The course improves familiarity with the format and content of IELTS Academic and General Training and trains the four skills (listening, reading, writing, speaking) with exam strategies and practice.

It suits final-year school students and university students who need a specific score for admission or scholarships abroad. Candidates can also take a free IELTS familiarisation (practice) test online and book the real exam with the British Council in Georgia.
highlights: Taught by the organisation that co-owns IELTS
Exam strategies for all four skills
Can be combined with IELTS registration in Tbilisi
british-council-georgia-ielts-prep-young.eligibility: Young adults (typically 16+) with at least intermediate English.
how_to_apply: Open the British Council Georgia English courses page
Book a free consultation or check the IELTS preparation course page
Register online for the next intake and pay the fee
british-council-georgia-ielts-prep-young.costs: Paid; course fee published on the course page or given at consultation (the IELTS exam fee is separate).

british-council-georgia-secondary-englis.about:
The British Council in Georgia runs English courses for children and teenagers at its Tbilisi teaching centre and online. The Secondary English course (11–17 years) builds communication, confidence and academic English; related options include a Grammar and Vocabulary Coach, Cambridge English exam preparation for teens and live online Secondary English classes.

Courses follow the school academic year and are taught by British Council teachers. Families start by booking a free consultation, where an adviser checks the learner's level and recommends a course; registration is then done online in four steps. A strong option for students preparing for Cambridge exams, IELTS later on, or study abroad.
highlights: Taught by British Council teachers in Tbilisi or live online
Cambridge exam preparation track for teens
Free consultation and level check before enrolling
british-council-georgia-secondary-englis.eligibility: Learners aged 11–17; level assessed at consultation.
how_to_apply: Visit the British Council Georgia 'English courses for kids and teens' page
Book a free consultation
Take the level check and choose a course and schedule
Register online and pay the course fee
british-council-georgia-secondary-englis.costs: Paid; fees depend on course and are given on the course pages or at consultation.

cu-cybersecurity-ai-in-education-confere.about:
Caucasus University's School of Technology hosts an international hybrid conference, 'Cybersecurity and Artificial Intelligence (AI) in Education', organised by the Scientific Cyber Security Association and Educational Technologies, with partners Sulakauri Publishing and the Georgian AI Association (GAIA). It takes place on 7 November 2026 from 10:30.

The programme includes an interactive panel on cybersecurity, deepfakes, voice cloning, AI ethics and digital hygiene, with experts answering participants' questions. School teachers and pupils in grades 5–12 can register as speakers and present their own topic, or attend as listeners in person or online. All attendees receive a participation certificate; teachers and pupils who present also receive the status of 'Digital Education and Safety Ambassador'. A good first conference-speaking experience for school students interested in tech.
highlights: Pupils in grades 5–12 can present their own talk
Certificates for all; 'Digital Education and Safety Ambassador' status for speakers
Hybrid: attend at Caucasus University in Tbilisi or online
cu-cybersecurity-ai-in-education-confere.eligibility: School pupils in grades 5–12, teachers and anyone interested; working language Georgian.
how_to_apply: Open the event page on cu.edu.ge
Fill in the registration form and choose 'speaker' or 'listener'
If presenting, prepare a short talk on cybersecurity or AI in education
Receive the agenda by email a few days before 7 November and attend on site or online

egoi-georgia-team-selection-2027.about:
The Georgian Tech Olympiads Hub, a joint project of TBC Bank and Business and Technology University (BTU), runs Georgia's national selection for the European Girls' Olympiad in Informatics (EGOI). EGOI encourages girls into computer science: each country sends a team of four girls who solve hard algorithmic problems individually in two five-hour contest days.

The Georgian selection mirrors the international format: two rounds of three problems in five hours each, held on the BTU campus in Tbilisi. The four best girls form the national team (with two reserves) and attend a 20-day intensive training camp before travelling to EGOI; participation, training and team travel are organised by the Hub. Solid programming skills plus algorithms and data structures are required.
highlights: Path to an international olympiad for girls in programming
20-day pre-olympiad training camp for the selected team
Free selection rounds at BTU, Tbilisi
egoi-georgia-team-selection-2027.eligibility: Girls under 18 who are school students in Georgia; strong programming, algorithms and data-structures skills needed.
how_to_apply: Watch the Georgian Tech Olympiads Hub page on TBC's website in late February 2027
Fill in the Google Form registration between 1 and 31 March 2027
Sit the two selection rounds at BTU
If selected, join the 20-day training camp and travel with the team to EGOI
egoi-georgia-team-selection-2027.costs: Free; team training and participation organised by the Hub (TBC Bank and BTU).

eiec-environmental-agrarian-webinars-sch.about:
The EIEC, Georgia's state centre for environmental education, offers free webinars throughout the year for school students, teachers and other interested groups on environmental and agricultural topics such as climate change, biodiversity, waste, water and sustainable farming.

A school, club or youth group chooses a topic and the centre plans the webinar for the right age group. It is an easy way for an eco-club or class to bring in an expert speaker.
highlights: Free expert session for your class or club
Choose the topic and age level
Available all year
eiec-environmental-agrarian-webinars-sch.eligibility: School classes, eco-clubs, teachers and other groups in Georgia; sessions in Georgian.
how_to_apply: Open the webinars page on eiec.gov.ge
Use the registration link to request a webinar, stating topic, group and age
Agree the date with the centre

eiec-environmental-democracy-e-learning-.about:
The Environmental Information and Education Centre (EIEC), a public body under Georgia's Ministry of Environmental Protection and Agriculture, offers a free online course on environmental democracy - the first of its kind in Georgian.

The course has two modules and aims to strengthen knowledge of environmental rights and responsibilities and of how the public can participate in environmental decision-making (access to information, consultations, appeals). It suits school students, university students, activists and anyone interested in environmental policy.

Registration is online at any time via the EIEC course page.
highlights: Free, online and self-paced
Learn how to use environmental rights in practice
Good grounding for law, policy and environmental studies
eiec-environmental-democracy-e-learning-.eligibility: Anyone who reads Georgian; no prerequisites.
how_to_apply: Open the course page on eiec.gov.ge
Click the registration link and create your account
Complete the two modules at your own pace

eiec-green-camp-climate-ambassadors-2027.about:
Green Camp "Climate Ambassadors" is run by Georgia's Environmental Information and Education Centre to raise young people's awareness of environmental issues and prepare them to implement projects locally after the camp.

The programme covers forest management, biodiversity, atmospheric air quality, climate change and disaster risk reduction, community-based disaster risk management, Georgia's geological hazards and the role of the National Environmental Agency's hydrometeorology department. Participants work with specialists on topics that interest them and take part in team activities.

The camp runs annually; watch the EIEC youth programmes page for the next call.
highlights: Learn from Georgia's environmental specialists
Team activities and hands-on topics
Become a local Climate Ambassador
eiec-green-camp-climate-ambassadors-2027.eligibility: Young people in Georgia (age range set in each year's call); sessions in Georgian.
how_to_apply: Follow the EIEC youth programmes page for the next call
Apply with the published form
If selected, attend the camp and then run a local project

eiec-soil-essay-contest-human-footprint-.about:
The Environmental Information and Education Centre (EIEC), the environmental education agency of Georgia's Ministry of Environmental Protection and Agriculture, runs this essay contest for World Soil Day (5 December). The 2026 campaign theme is soil compaction: 'Stop soil compaction, increase soil productivity'. Pupils are asked what footprint people leave on soil and what soil we should leave to future generations.

It is open to pupils of general schools anywhere in Georgia in two categories: grades 7-9 and grades 10-12. Essays of 300-600 words in Georgian (Word or PDF, Sylfaen 12, 1.5 spacing) must describe the problem and its causes, give examples, state your own opinion and propose solutions, with sources cited. A jury scores out of 100, rewarding depth of understanding (25), argument (20) and independent thinking (20) over the amount of information.

Winners in 1st-3rd place in each category receive certificates named after academician Tengiz Urushadze at a ceremony on 5 December 2026. A quick, free entry for pupils interested in environment, agriculture or biology.
highlights: Two categories: grades 7-9 and 10-12
Short essay (300-600 words), entry by email
Award ceremony on World Soil Day, 5 December
eiec-soil-essay-contest-human-footprint-.eligibility: Pupils in grades 7-12 of general education schools in Georgia. Essays must be in Georgian and the pupil's own work.
how_to_apply: Read the contest conditions on eiec.gov.ge
Write a 300-600 word essay in Georgian (Word or PDF, Sylfaen 12, 1.5 spacing) with sources
Email it to info@eiec.gov.ge by 20 November 2026 with your name, surname, school, contact details and a short description of the work

eiec-young-volunteers-network-2027.about:
The Young Volunteers Network of Georgia's Environmental Information and Education Centre brings together young people aged 15-17 and supports their active involvement in educational activities at local level.

Volunteers gain knowledge and experience, develop skills and make friends while contributing to sustainable development. Topics include communication and presentation skills, the Sustainable Development Goals, climate change and its risks, biodiversity, forest and water management, renewable energy, waste management and ecosystem services.

Members are selected through an annual call; the 2026 cohort is active, so watch the EIEC youth programmes page for the next intake.
highlights: Training in climate, biodiversity, energy and waste
Lead real activities in your community
Volunteering record for university applications
eiec-young-volunteers-network-2027.eligibility: Young people aged 15-17 living in Georgia; activities in Georgian.
how_to_apply: Follow the EIEC youth programmes page and social media for the next call
Apply through the form published with the call
Join the training and start local activities

finedu-nbg-visit-school-finance-clubs-20.about:
FinEdu, the financial-education platform of the National Bank of Georgia (NBG), invites school financial-education clubs to information and training sessions at the NBG headquarters in Tbilisi. The project is designed for pupils in grades 8–12 and aims to strengthen interest in financial literacy and personal money-management skills.

Each two-hour session on the theme 'From wishes to financial independence' combines short theory, practical exercises, discussion and fun activities. Sessions are scheduled for November–December 2026. The club's leader (usually a teacher) registers the club through FinEdu's online form; places are limited and allocated in order of registration, and the form closes when full.
highlights: Visit the central bank of Georgia with your school club
Hands-on activities on budgeting and personal finance
Free; places allocated first come, first served
finedu-nbg-visit-school-finance-clubs-20.eligibility: School financial-education clubs in Georgia with pupils in grades 8–12; registration is done by the club leader. Sessions are in Georgian.
how_to_apply: Ask your teacher or club leader to open the FinEdu announcement
The club leader completes the registration form linked on the page
Wait for FinEdu to confirm the session date
Attend the session at NBG headquarters in Tbilisi

genius-olympiad-georgia-national-selecti.about:
The GENIUS Olympiad is an international competition that asks young people to understand global environmental challenges and design scientific, technological and creative solutions. ROCO Academy is the official GENIUS representative in Georgia and, with the University of Georgia (UG) as host, runs a nationwide internal selection round.

The selection is open to pupils in grades 8–12 in five categories: Coding, Artificial Intelligence, Science, Entrepreneurship and Robotics (one category per student). Students pre-register (in the last cycle the deadline was 25 January), selected participants compete in the national round at UG in Tbilisi in March, and winners represent Georgia at the GENIUS Olympiad Global Finals in Rochester, USA, in June.
highlights: Five categories: coding, AI, science, entrepreneurship, robotics
Winners go to the Global Finals in Rochester, USA
Hosted at the University of Georgia in Tbilisi
genius-olympiad-georgia-national-selecti.eligibility: School students in grades 8–12 in Georgia; one category per student.
how_to_apply: Check UG's announcements and ROCO Academy channels from December 2026
Pre-register in one category before the January deadline (25 January in the last cycle)
Prepare your project or solution for the chosen category
Compete in the national selection round at UG in March 2027
genius-olympiad-georgia-national-selecti.costs: Selection round free per UG announcement; costs of the Global Finals trip are not stated.

georgia-ibo-team-selection-2027.about:
Every year Georgia's Ministry of Education, Science and Youth, through the Shota Rustaveli National Science Foundation, selects, trains and sends national teams to the priority international school olympiads, including the International Biology Olympiad (IBO).

Candidates are the strongest finishers of the National School Olympiad (run by the National Assessment and Examinations Center), chosen under the olympiad rules. They sit two selection rounds organised by the Foundation; the best become team members (plus reserves) and are trained by a team of Foundation coaches (leader, deputy leader and assistants). The Foundation administers and funds the delegation's participation abroad.

In 2026 the rules were issued on 13 March and the IBO rounds took place in April. To be considered for 2027, compete in the 2026-27 National School Olympiad in biology.
highlights: Route to represent Georgia at the IBO
Free coaching by the Foundation's team of trainers
Travel and participation fully funded
georgia-ibo-team-selection-2027.eligibility: School students in Georgia selected as candidates on the basis of National School Olympiad results in biology (and any age limits set by the IBO rules).
how_to_apply: Register for and compete in the 2026-27 National School Olympiad in biology
Reach the top finishers so you are invited as a team candidate
Submit the candidate application form when the Foundation publishes the 2027 rules (around March)
Sit the two selection rounds in spring 2027
If selected, train with the national team coaches
georgia-ibo-team-selection-2027.costs: Free. Training, travel and participation at the international olympiad are funded by the state through the Foundation.

georgia-mfa-paid-internships-embassies-a.about:
As part of the state paid internship programme initiated by Georgia's Prime Minister, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs is recruiting interns for three-month paid placements at Georgian diplomatic missions abroad, starting in 2027.

It is open to citizens of Georgia who are studying in, or have graduated from, an accredited bachelor's, master's or doctoral programme (higher or vocational education) abroad. Host missions include the embassies in Belgium, Spain, Germany, France, Italy, Greece, the Czech Republic, the UK, Denmark, Sweden, Norway, the Netherlands, Egypt, Qatar, Kuwait, the UAE, Jordan, the USA, Canada, the Holy See and China, plus the Permanent Missions to the UN in Geneva and New York. Pay is set under Georgian legislation.

Each mission publishes its own announcement (linked from the MFA notice); documents are sent to that mission's official email by 8 November 2026. It is a rare chance to gain diplomatic work experience in the city where you already study.
highlights: Paid diplomatic work experience at an embassy or UN mission
Placements in 20+ countries including Qatar, UAE and Kuwait
Part of a national state internship programme
georgia-mfa-paid-internships-embassies-a.eligibility: Citizens of Georgia studying at, or graduated from, an accredited bachelor's, master's or doctoral (or vocational) programme abroad. Other requirements are set by each mission's announcement.
how_to_apply: Open the MFA announcement and the linked notice of the mission in your country
Prepare the documents listed by that mission (CV, proof of study/graduation, etc.)
Email them to the mission's official address by 8 November 2026
Attend any interview the mission arranges
georgia-mfa-paid-internships-embassies-a.costs: Paid internship; the amount is set under Georgian legislation. No application fee.

georgia-red-cross-volunteering.about:
The Georgia Red Cross Society is the country's national Red Cross society and part of the world's largest humanitarian network. It reports around 15,000 registered volunteers, 39 branches and 27 social day centres across Georgia, and runs projects on mass immunisation support, diabetes prevention in Kvemo Kartli and disaster management, with support from the IFRC, ICRC and partner national societies.

Volunteers help in their own town or region: supporting social day centres and older people, first-aid and health-awareness activities, emergency and disaster preparedness, and fundraising or community events. Many school and university students start through Red Cross youth clubs (some schools have their own clubs). Volunteering builds first-aid skills, teamwork and a strong record of community service for university applications.
highlights: Nationwide network: 39 branches, about 15,000 volunteers
First-aid training and humanitarian experience
Year-round registration; volunteer close to home
georgia-red-cross-volunteering.eligibility: Open to residents of Georgia; minimum age and tasks depend on the branch (minors usually need parental consent). Georgian is useful for most activities.
how_to_apply: Open redcross.ge and go to 'Become a volunteer'
Complete the volunteer registration or contact the head office (+995 32 2 501 105, 71 Vazisubani St, Tbilisi)
Get referred to your local branch
Attend the induction and first-aid training, then join activities

georgia-science-and-innovation-festival-.about:
Since 2016 Georgia has held a Science and Innovation Festival every autumn, coordinated by the Shota Rustaveli National Science Foundation with the Ministry of Education. Universities, research centres, the National Academy of Sciences, museums, libraries and publishers across Georgia run public events.

Formats include conferences, public lectures, workshops, science-popular experiments, exhibitions, science cafes and shows, competitions, quizzes and special events for school students. Venues include university campuses, the Georgian National Museum and libraries in Tbilisi and the regions.

For students it is the easiest way to visit labs, meet researchers and try experiments for free; universities and schools can also propose events that showcase student research.
highlights: Free labs, lectures and science shows across Georgia
Special events for school students
Meet researchers and visit universities
georgia-science-and-innovation-festival-.eligibility: Open to the public; most events are free and walk-in. Institutions (universities, research centres, schools) can propose events.
how_to_apply: Check the festival page and Facebook from September 2027 for the programme
Pick events in your city (some need online registration)
Attend; teachers can book class visits where offered

goethe-institut-georgia-german-courses-y.about:
The Goethe-Institut Georgien in Tbilisi (Sandukeli St 16) offers German courses for children and young people aged 8–16, with age-appropriate topics and play-oriented teaching. Lessons follow the CEFR levels (A1 onwards) and take place 2–3 times a week in the classroom and via Zoom.

Learners who already know some German can take a free placement test to find the right level. The courses prepare young learners for Goethe-Institut exams (Fit in Deutsch and the Goethe-Zertifikat), which are useful for German partner schools, youth exchanges and later study in Germany.
highlights: Official Goethe-Institut teaching in Tbilisi
Free placement test
Pathway to Goethe exams and study in Germany
how_to_apply: Open the Goethe-Institut Georgia German courses page
Take the free placement test if you already know some German
Choose a course for children and young people and enrol via 'Contact and enrolment'
Pay the course fee before the course starts
goethe-institut-georgia-german-courses-y.costs: Paid; fees per course level are listed by the Goethe-Institut Georgien.

iliauni-black-sea-caucasus-summer-school.about:
Ilia State University's International Summer School 'Black Sea and Caucasus: Diversity, Conflicts and Networks' brings students from around the world to its main campus in Tbilisi for four weeks. The course examines the region's cultural, political and economic dimensions (Armenia, Azerbaijan, Belarus, Georgia, Moldova, Türkiye and Ukraine), including recent conflicts, cooperation patterns, security and development, taught by Ilia faculty with guest speakers such as Harvard's Davis Center and the U.S. Embassy in Tbilisi. Participants also study Georgian, Ukrainian or Russian.

The package includes tuition, serviced accommodation, insurance, airport transfer, a welcome pack, cultural activities and field trips (Kazbegi, Kakheti, Batumi, Mtskheta and Gori), most meals and certificates. In 2026 it ran 29 June – 26 July with an early-bird deadline of 1 April and a main deadline of 1 May; the 2027 edition is expected to follow the same calendar. Excellent for international relations, history and regional-studies students who want a first-hand look at the Caucasus.
highlights: Study the Black Sea and Caucasus region on the ground in Tbilisi
Language course in Georgian, Ukrainian or Russian included
Field trips to Kazbegi, Kakheti, Batumi and Mtskheta
iliauni-black-sea-caucasus-summer-school.eligibility: Full-time university students aged 18+ who have completed at least one semester, with good English; open to all nationalities.
how_to_apply: Check the summer school page for 2027 dates
Prepare passport/ID, CV, cover letter, proof of enrolment, a recommendation letter and an English certificate (if not a native speaker)
Submit the online application form (early bird by about 1 April, main deadline about 1 May)
Pay the programme fee after admission
iliauni-black-sea-caucasus-summer-school.costs: 2026 fee: USD 3,600–4,000 depending on single or double room, covering tuition, accommodation, insurance, transfers, trips and most meals; airfare and dinners not included; 5% early-bird discount.

iliauni-kirkland-programme-day-2026.about:
Ilia State University hosts a Kirkland Programme Day dedicated to the Lane Kirkland Scholarship Program, a Polish-funded programme that brings young professionals, graduates and researchers from Georgia and other partner countries to Polish universities for study, research and practical experience.

The event presents the programme's opportunities and application procedure, includes an interactive Q&A session and 'Kirkland Open Space', where participants meet alumni informally and discuss academic and professional plans. It is useful for students, graduates, young professionals and researchers considering study or research in Poland. Working language: English; in person on 4 November 2026, 10:00–14:00, Ilia State University hall G106 (Tsereteli Ave. 1-3, Tbilisi).
highlights: Meet Lane Kirkland alumni and ask about applying
Learn the application procedure for study and research in Poland
Free, in English, with networking in 'Kirkland Open Space'
iliauni-kirkland-programme-day-2026.eligibility: Open to students, graduates, young professionals, researchers and civil-society staff; English is the working language. Prior registration required.
how_to_apply: Open the event announcement on the Ilia State University website
Fill in the registration form linked in the announcement
Attend on 4 November 2026 at 10:00 in hall G106, Ilia State University, Tbilisi

iliauni-public-speaking-communication-co.about:
Ilia State University's Centre for Personal and Professional Development, together with the Faculty of Arts and Sciences and the IliaUni Theatre, runs a certificate course called 'The Art of Public Speaking and Communication'. The programme combines psychology, body-oriented practice and drama: participants work on the theatre stage to overcome speaking anxiety, build confidence, express ideas clearly and convincingly, and influence an audience.

The course is led by Saba Chikhladze (MA in organisational psychology) and runs for four weeks at the IliaUni Theatre in Tbilisi, with eight two-hour sessions between 24 November and 19 December 2026 (evening and Saturday afternoon slots). It suits university students, graduates and young professionals who want practical speaking skills for debate, MUN, interviews or presentations; teaching is in Georgian.
highlights: Practical public-speaking training on a real theatre stage
Combines psychology, body-based practice and drama techniques
Ilia State University certificate; fee can be paid in instalments
iliauni-public-speaking-communication-co.eligibility: Open to anyone interested (students, graduates, professionals); taught in Georgian, so participants need a working command of Georgian.
how_to_apply: Read the announcement on the Ilia State University news page
Submit an application via the link or contact given in the announcement before 20 November 2026
Arrange payment of the course fee (instalments possible)
Attend the first session on 24 November 2026 at the IliaUni Theatre
iliauni-public-speaking-communication-co.costs: Fee: 600 GEL for the whole course (can be split into instalments).

komarovi-saturday-school-maths-logic-202.about:
Komarovi School (Tbilisi Physics and Mathematics Public School No. 199) has run its 'Saturday School' for about 20 years. It is a weekly maths and logic programme for pupils in grades 3–6 who enjoy mathematics: one three-hour lesson a week, groups of 17–20, specially compiled problem books given free to students, and game-based teaching for the youngest.

The school year is split into three modules of 12 lessons; each module ends with a summative test, and Saturday School pupils take part in the school's grade-5 and grade-6 maths olympiads. Besides the main campus (49 Vazha-Pshavela Ave), new Tbilisi branches opened in October 2026 at Prometheus school (Mukhiani, Saturdays) and SEU (Isani, Sundays), and the programme also runs in more than 20 regional towns including Batumi, Gori, Zugdidi, Telavi, Rustavi and Mtskheta. It is a respected early pathway to olympiad maths and to Komarovi's competitive entrance exam.
highlights: Olympiad-style maths and logic from a top Georgian physics-maths school
Branches across Tbilisi and 20+ regional towns
Free problem books, small groups, end-of-module tests and olympiads
komarovi-saturday-school-maths-logic-202.eligibility: Pupils in grades 3–6 with an interest in mathematics; taught in Georgian.
how_to_apply: Read the Saturday School pages on komarovi.edu.ge
Fill in the registration form of your branch (links in the October 2026 announcement) or contact the branch manager
Agree the group and payment with the branch
Attend weekly lessons; take the module-end tests
komarovi-saturday-school-maths-logic-202.costs: New students: 600 GEL per module (12 lessons, 3 months); sibling discount (300 GEL per module for each additional child).

national-bank-of-georgia-student-interns.about:
Georgia's central bank runs an internship (practice) track for students alongside its vacancies. On the career section of nbg.gov.ge, applicants select the category or department where they would like to intern (for example monetary policy, financial stability, supervision, statistics, legal, IT) and upload their academic transcript and CV.

There is no fixed call window: applications are kept and matched to department needs. It suits economics, finance, law, statistics and computer science students who want real experience at the country's main economic institution.
highlights: Experience inside Georgia's central bank
Choose the department you want
Apply any time online
national-bank-of-georgia-student-interns.eligibility: University students (and recent graduates) able to work in Georgian; specific requirements depend on the department.
how_to_apply: Open the internships page on nbg.gov.ge
Select the area where you want to intern
Upload your transcript and CV and submit
Wait to be contacted if a department has a place
national-bank-of-georgia-student-interns.costs: No application fee; compensation is not stated on the page.

startupbootcamp-georgia-dare-to-build-20.about:
'Dare to Build' is the MVP stage of Startupbootcamp Georgia, the GITA-funded accelerator delivered by the Rainmaking group. It is for founders who have validated a problem and are ready to turn that insight into a working product.

From 18 March to 2 July 2027, about 20 founders or teams create an MVP roadmap, build and test the product with users, and strengthen financial, legal, branding and pitching foundations. Each selected startup receives a GEL 50,000 grant from GITA and no equity is taken. Selection looks at the team's commitment, evidence of customer discovery, solution scope, early business-model thinking and openness to mentorship.
highlights: GEL 50,000 non-dilutive grant from GITA
Mentoring from Startupbootcamp's global network
Build and test an MVP with real customers
startupbootcamp-georgia-dare-to-build-20.eligibility: Tech-enabled startups in any sector; the company must be registered in Georgia before joining (founders of any nationality can register a Georgian company). Previous GITA grant recipients who received more than GEL 100,000 are not eligible; the same founders may reapply only with a different company. English and Georgian used.
how_to_apply: Read the Dare to Build page
Prepare evidence of customer discovery and problem validation
Submit the application form by 31 January 2027
Hear back the week of 8 March 2027
startupbootcamp-georgia-dare-to-build-20.costs: Free to join; GEL 50,000 grant per startup; no equity taken.

startupbootcamp-georgia-dare-to-grow-202.about:
'Dare to Grow' is the most advanced stage of Startupbootcamp Georgia, funded by GITA and delivered by the Rainmaking group. It is for startups with a product or MVP that are ready to find customers, enter markets and prepare for investment.

From 12 July to 16 December 2027, 10 startups optimise their MVP and market-entry approach, build customer acquisition, sales and retention systems, assess international expansion and strengthen fundraising materials before pitching to investors. Each receives a GEL 150,000 grant from GITA with no equity taken. Selection weighs team strength, traction, market opportunity, product readiness, business model and growth ambition.
highlights: GEL 150,000 non-dilutive grant from GITA
Focus on first revenue, international markets and investor readiness
Small cohort of 10 startups
startupbootcamp-georgia-dare-to-grow-202.eligibility: Tech-enabled startups in any sector; the company must be registered in Georgia before joining (founders of any nationality can register a Georgian company). Previous GITA grant recipients who received more than GEL 100,000 are not eligible; the same founders may reapply only with a different company. English and Georgian used.
how_to_apply: Read the Dare to Grow page
Gather traction data (users, pilots, revenue)
Submit the application by 23 May 2027
Hear back the week of 28 June 2027
startupbootcamp-georgia-dare-to-grow-202.costs: Free to join; GEL 150,000 grant per startup; no equity taken.

startupbootcamp-georgia-dare-to-start-20.about:
Startupbootcamp Georgia is a GITA-funded accelerator run by the Rainmaking group, adapting Startupbootcamp's global playbooks, mentors and investor networks to founders building from Georgia. 'Dare to Start' is its first stage, the Founder-Market Fit Programme, for people who have an idea or a problem worth exploring.

Over two months (12 January – 2 March 2027, hybrid), about 40 solo founders or teams define the problem and customer segment, research the market, and use customer discovery to test whether their solution direction is worth building. Applications are scored on founder qualities, problem clarity, market potential, execution potential and programme fit. Graduates can move on to 'Dare to Build' (MVP stage, GEL 50,000 grant) and 'Dare to Grow' (GEL 150,000 grant). A strong first step for student and young founders.
highlights: Free, structured idea-validation programme with Startupbootcamp mentors
Path to later GITA-funded stages with GEL 50,000–150,000 non-dilutive grants
Hybrid format; about 40 founders per cohort
startupbootcamp-georgia-dare-to-start-20.eligibility: Tech-enabled startups in any sector; the company must be registered in Georgia before joining (founders of any nationality can register a Georgian company). Previous GITA grant recipients who received more than GEL 100,000 are not eligible; the same founders may reapply only with a different company. English and Georgian used.
how_to_apply: Read the Dare to Start page and use the online stage finder if unsure
Submit the application form (tally.so) by 27 November 2026
Make sure your company can be registered in Georgia before the programme starts
Hear back the week of 7 December 2026; programme starts 12 January 2027

tsu-envoy-ambassador-programme-2027.about:
'TSU Envoy' (TSU Despani) is a project of TSU's Children's University that has run for 13 seasons. Students at any level (bachelor's, master's, PhD, vocational or the 60-credit teacher programme) return to their own former school and present TSU's study programmes and student life to senior pupils, helping them choose a university and profession.

Before visiting schools, registered envoys complete training in presentation skills (in the 2026 season, 26 January – 13 February). The project promotes volunteering and non-formal education and is supported by the Ministry of Education, Science and Youth. Each participant receives a certificate of participation, which can be used in TSU scholarship competitions. Contact: tsuenvoy@tsu.ge.
highlights: Presentation-skills training before school visits
Certificate usable in scholarship competitions
Give back to your own school and mentor younger pupils
tsu-envoy-ambassador-programme-2027.eligibility: Students of Ivane Javakhishvili Tbilisi State University at any level; teaching in Georgian.
how_to_apply: Watch the TSU Children's University news page in December 2026
Register through the form in the 'TSU Envoy 2027' announcement
Attend the presentation-skills training
Visit your former school and present TSU programmes to senior pupils

ug-comparative-criminal-law-training-202.about:
The Georgian, German and International Criminal Law Institute of the University of Georgia (UG) runs a competitive call for a one-day training, 'Comparative Criminal Law – German and Georgian Perspectives'. It is taught by Professor Martin Wasmeier (University of Cologne), Associate Professor Özdem Özaydın (Istanbul Kültür University and Ruhr University Bochum) and Professor Bachana Jishkariani (UG).

The training takes place on 27 November 2026, 12:00–17:00, in the conference hall (room 519) of UG, 77a Kostava Street, Tbilisi. It is free; the working language is German with Georgian interpretation. Participants who attend the whole session receive a certificate. It is a good way for law students to meet German academics and explore criminal-law study or research in Germany.
highlights: Taught by professors from the University of Cologne, Ruhr University Bochum and UG
Free, with a certificate for full attendance
Open to law students from all accredited Georgian universities
ug-comparative-criminal-law-training-202.eligibility: Law students from any accredited university in Georgia from the second year of bachelor's study, plus master's and PhD students; a limited number of practising lawyers. Georgian interpretation is provided, so German is not required.
how_to_apply: Prepare a CV and a motivation letter
Email them to institute.criminallaw@gmail.com by 15 November 2026
Wait for confirmation of selection
Attend on 27 November 2026 at UG, 77a Kostava Street, room 519

ug-illuminate-plus-legal-english-course-.about:
The TOLES Legal English Centre Georgia at the University of Georgia offers Illuminate Plus, a practical Legal English course for students and legal professionals. Based on the TOLES/Cambridge Law Studio curriculum, its 10 modules cover contract formation, commercial contract clauses, business liability, warranties, damages for breach of contract and the structure of commercial agreements.

The course suits learners with B1–B2 English, improves legal terminology and analysis of legal texts, and prepares for all three levels of the TOLES Legal English exam. It runs for five weeks (two 2.5-hour sessions per week, 25 hours in total) at UG in Tbilisi, led by lecturer Tsira Chorgoliani. The fee includes one year of access to the Illuminate Plus online platform, a TOLES/Cambridge Law Studio certificate and a UG certificate.
highlights: TOLES/Cambridge Law Studio curriculum and certificate
Prepares for all three TOLES Legal English exam levels
One year of online platform access included
ug-illuminate-plus-legal-english-course-.eligibility: Law students and legal professionals with B1–B2 English.
how_to_apply: Email your CV to toles_info@ug.edu.ge by 8 November 2026
Confirm your place and payment schedule with the centre
Attend the 10 sessions at UG, Tbilisi
ug-illuminate-plus-legal-english-course-.costs: Fee: 900 GEL, payable in three instalments of 300 GEL; includes platform access and certificates.

zugdidi-youth-projects-cofunding.about:
Zugdidi municipality (Samegrelo) funds projects that organisations run with and for local young people aged 14-29, both residents and internally displaced persons. Themes include healthy lifestyles, gender equality, youth entrepreneurship, personal development through non-formal education, inclusive education and other projects that meet young people's needs and Georgia's youth policy goals.

Projects costing up to 2,000 GEL can be funded in full; between 2,000 and 5,000 GEL the City Hall co-funds up to 90%. A commission usually meets in the first week of each month and the applicant presents the project (online attendance allowed). Each organisation can use the programme once a year, and a report with photos, a participant list and proof of spending is due within a month after the project.

Useful for student clubs, youth NGOs and school-based initiative groups in Zugdidi that need a first grant for a camp, training, exchange or campaign.
highlights: Up to 5,000 GEL; projects up to 2,000 GEL fully funded
Monthly commission, rolling applications
Projects can also take local youth to events outside Zugdidi or abroad
zugdidi-youth-projects-cofunding.eligibility: Organisations working in the youth field (NGOs and similar legal entities) whose project targets young people aged 14-29 registered in Zugdidi municipality (local or IDP), ideally at least about 25 participants. Documents in Georgian.
how_to_apply: Read the rules on the programme page on zugdidi.gov.ge and download the application annex
Prepare: application to the Mayor, project form with budget and plan, public registry extract, representative's ID, bank details, and parental consent if minors travel outside Zugdidi
Submit to Zugdidi City Hall (hotline 591 54 40 44, info@zugdidi.gov.ge)
Present the project at the commission meeting (in person or online)
Run the project and report within one month
zugdidi-youth-projects-cofunding.costs: Free to apply. Up to 5,000 GEL per project (full funding up to 2,000 GEL; up to 90% co-funding above that).

cmuq-qatar-mathematics-research-forum.about:
The Qatar Mathematics Research Forum (QMRF) is a touchpoint for mathematicians, researchers and students from institutions across Qatar to exchange ideas, learn about each other's research and explore collaboration. It also gives students and early-career researchers a way into the wider mathematical community, with plans for joint seminars, workshops and scientific meetings.

Seminars take place at CMU-Q in Education City (Room 1213, 1:00-2:00 pm). Recent and upcoming talks include Dr Hassan Hachem (HBKU) on degradation dynamics (27 October 2026) and Dr Aline Abassian (UDST) on mathematical modelling in mathematics education (17 November 2026).
highlights: Meet mathematicians from all Qatar universities
Free, one-hour talks
Good for students considering maths research
cmuq-qatar-mathematics-research-forum.eligibility: Students, researchers and professionals interested in mathematics; university students especially welcome.
how_to_apply: Check the QMRF page for the next seminar
Contact the organiser if attending for the first time
Attend at CMU-Q in Education City

cmuq-university-lectures.about:
CMU-Q's University Lectures bring some of the world's most thoughtful people to Education City to lead public conversations on technology, sustainability, business, science, government policy and strategic planning. Formats include the Dean's Lecture, Dean's Panel and Distinguished Lecture series, held throughout the academic year.

They are a free way for high school and university students in Doha to hear world-class speakers, ask questions and experience a Carnegie Mellon campus. Upcoming lectures and registration links are posted on CMU-Q's events page.
highlights: World-class speakers in Doha
Free and open to the public
Great exposure to a top university campus
cmuq-university-lectures.eligibility: Open to the public, including high school and university students.
how_to_apply: Check CMU-Q's events page for upcoming lectures
Register for the lecture (if required)
Attend in Education City

hbku-student-enrichment-program.about:
HBKU's Student Enrichment Program ('LEAD: Learn. Engage. Aspire. Distinguish.') equips undergraduate and graduate engineering students with skills to stand out in their careers, bridging academic knowledge and industry needs. Focus areas are management and leadership, emerging technologies, and innovation and entrepreneurship.

Services include short technical and non-technical courses (half a day to five days) during semester breaks, internationally recognised certifications, hackathons, one-on-one consultations, awareness programmes and experiential learning with industry partners. Activities are recorded on the official Student Involvement Record.
highlights: Industry certifications for free
Hackathons and emerging-tech courses
Recorded on your Student Involvement Record
hbku-student-enrichment-program.eligibility: Undergraduate and graduate engineering students at HBKU.
how_to_apply: Check the Student Enrichment Program page each semester
Register for courses or hackathons
Book a one-on-one consultation

qsc-car-mechanics-centre.about:
The Car Mechanics Centre is a fully air-conditioned, safety-certified facility equipped with specialist engine equipment, training rooms and a lounge. It trains members in two core tracks, car mechanics and car electrics, at beginner, hobbyist and professional levels, and promotes safe motorsport through supervised car preparation and regular safe-racing events at approved tracks.

Facilities include a car workshop, a motorcycle workshop, lifts of various sizes and a driving simulator. Members must be 15 or older.
highlights: Hands-on engine and electrics training
Motorbike workshop and driving simulator
Safe-racing events
how_to_apply: Register as a QSC member online
Choose a car mechanics or car electrics programme
Attend training at the centre
qsc-car-mechanics-centre.costs: Check with QSC; many programmes free or low-cost.

qsc-makers-oasis.about:
Makers' Oasis is a group of hand and digital fabrication labs at the Qatar Scientific Club, equipped with modern measuring and manufacturing tools so that members of the community can design, build and innovate quickly and cheaply. It covers five specialisations: design, manufacturing, electronics, software and production mechanics, with workshops for engineering design, fabrication and assembly, CNC cutting, electronics, metal forming and woodwork.

It welcomes everyone aged 15 and above, offering training and exchange between hobbyists and specialists. Students can use it to build science-fair projects, robots or startup prototypes.
highlights: CNC, electronics, metal and wood workshops
Expert help to turn ideas into prototypes
Open to everyone 15+
qsc-makers-oasis.eligibility: Members of the community aged 15+ in Qatar.
how_to_apply: Register as a member on the QSC website
Book a visit or training to use the labs
Bring your project and work with the lab specialists
qsc-makers-oasis.costs: Membership and training mostly free; some courses have fees.

qsc-promising-innovator-centre.about:
The Promising Innovator Centre attracts young members to technology and introduces scientific and engineering concepts through an accredited STEM curriculum of workshops and applied projects, plus hand and digital fabrication skills. It aims to discover and support talented children, build a culture of making and prototyping, and encourage scientific research and innovation.

Facilities include applied-science labs (chemistry, biology, physics and mathematics), a fab lab, a 'smart zone' for electronics, robotics and IT, and a 3D science dome for earth and space science. It serves boys and girls aged 7-14.
highlights: Real labs for chemistry, biology and physics
Robotics and electronics for children
3D science dome
qsc-promising-innovator-centre.eligibility: Girls and boys aged 7-14 in Qatar.
how_to_apply: Register your child on the QSC website (parent registration available)
Choose workshops or membership
Attend sessions at the centre
qsc-promising-innovator-centre.costs: Many activities free; some workshops charge a fee.

qstp-pitch-to-the-300-2026.about:
Pitch to The 300 is the second Investor-Startup Connect organised by QSTP's The 300, an initiative that educates and empowers women in Qatar to invest in high-potential startups and co-invest in Qatar-based ventures. Founders pitch at 3:30 pm, followed by questions, coffee and conversation, at the QSTP Incubation Center in Education City.

For student and early-stage founders it is a chance to practise a pitch in front of real investors and meet Qatar's growing angel community; attendees can also register just to learn how investors evaluate startups.
highlights: Pitch to real angel investors
Free registration
Networking at QSTP Incubation Center
qstp-pitch-to-the-300-2026.eligibility: Founders and startup-curious students and professionals in Qatar.
how_to_apply: Open the event page
Register through the form
Attend on 3 November at QSTP

acadia-entrance-scholarships-2027.about:
Acadia University in Wolfville, Nova Scotia, a small undergraduate-focused university, automatically considers Canadian and international applicants for initial entrance scholarships (CA$500–2,500) when they apply. Students with averages of 95%+ can receive renewable Chancellor's (CA$40,000 over four years), Board of Governors (CA$32,000) or President's (CA$28,000) scholarships, and some scholar-bursaries reach CA$80,000. The Raymond E. Ivany Merit Award is open to international first-years.

You need at least an 80% average (international grades are scaled) and must be within five years of finishing high school. After receiving your offer, complete the scholarship application in the Status Portal by 1 March.
highlights: Renewable awards up to CA$40,000
International students automatically considered
Scholarship application by 1 Mar 2027
acadia-entrance-scholarships-2027.eligibility: Canadian and international first-year (or early transfer) applicants with 80%+ average. Some named awards are domestic only. Georgia and Qatar citizens may apply.
how_to_apply: Apply to Acadia and submit documents
Receive your offer (with any initial award)
Complete the scholarship application in the Status Portal by 1 March 2027
Apply separately for named awards if eligible
acadia-entrance-scholarships-2027.costs: CA$500–2,500 initial awards; renewable CA$28,000–40,000 for 95%+ averages.

ajou-frontier-scholarship-international-.about:
Ajou University in Suwon selects admitted international students internally for Frontier Scholarships: S (100% tuition for 4 years), A (2 years), J (1 year), O (1 semester) and U (from one semester to four years, for applicants from OECD DAC aid-recipient countries with no current Ajou students, or those affected by war or disaster).

Global Scholarships for first-semester students waive 100% (TOPIK 6, IELTS 8.0 or TOEFL 100), 70% (TOPIK 5/IELTS 7.0/TOEFL 90), 50% or 30% of tuition depending on language scores. There is no separate application; selection is based on admission results. Ajou admits international students for spring and fall.
highlights: Up to 4 years of free tuition
English scores alone can earn 30–100% off
No separate application
ajou-frontier-scholarship-international-.eligibility: International freshmen, transfer and dual-degree students admitted to Ajou. Frontier U favours OECD DAC aid-recipient countries (Georgia qualifies). All nationalities for Global Scholarships.
how_to_apply: Apply in Ajou's international admission round (spring or fall 2027)
Submit TOPIK/IELTS/TOEFL scores with the application
Scholarships are assigned internally after admission
ajou-frontier-scholarship-international-.costs: 30–100% tuition waivers from one semester up to four years.

alabama-automatic-merit-scholarships-int.about:
The University of Alabama in Tuscaloosa applies the same automatic merit scale to out-of-state and international freshmen. With a 3.5+ GPA, awards rise with your official SAT or ACT score: Crimson Legends $6,000/year (SAT 1200–1250), Capstone $8,000, Collegiate $10,000, Foundation in Excellence $15,000, UA Scholar $24,000 (1360–1410), Presidential $28,000 (1420+), and Presidential Elite (1600/ACT 36, 4.0 GPA) covering tuition plus first-year housing and extra stipends.

There is no separate form: the scholarship is part of the UA undergraduate application. To be considered for summer/fall 2027 you must apply and send official test scores by 4 December 2026; later applicants are considered only if funds remain. UA does not superscore.
highlights: $6,000/year to full tuition, automatic
Strong SAT (1420+) gives $28,000/year
Apply with official scores by 4 Dec 2026
alabama-automatic-merit-scholarships-int.eligibility: International first-year applicants with a 3.5+ GPA and official SAT/ACT scores in the award bands. All nationalities, including Georgia and Qatar.
how_to_apply: Take the SAT or ACT and send official scores to UA
Submit the UA undergraduate application by 4 December 2026
Include GPA through junior year
Receive automatic award notification after admission
alabama-automatic-merit-scholarships-int.costs: $6,000–$28,000 per year for four years, or full tuition (Presidential Elite). International tuition is about $34,000/year.
